title: Microsoft Teams: improvements to the activity in other accounts and orgs panel
summary: The roadmap details and the documented preview behaviour check out, including the desktop sign-in policy. The briefing should acknowledge the general Teams licence requirement, qualify the notification limit, and avoid claiming that viewing other tenants' activity previously required switching tenants.

claims.where: What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not identify what the roadmap's improvements change compared with the documented preview panel.
claims.quote: Searched: '"activity in other accounts" improvements 577901 rollout prerequisites'; opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/activity-in-other-accounts-orgs. It describes the preview panel, not a delta for the improvements.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default state and required admin action for the roadmap improvements at general availability are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams activity in other accounts orgs panel default disable admin policy PowerShell Graph guest tenants improvements' and '"activity in other accounts" "policy" "default"'; read the roadmap and preview page. Neither specifies the GA improvements' default.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No panel-specific tenant admin switch, Teams PowerShell setting or Graph setting is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams activity in other accounts orgs panel default disable admin policy PowerShell Graph guest tenants improvements', '"activity in other accounts" "Graph"', '"activity in other accounts" "PowerShell"'; opened panel and Set-CsTeamsClientConfiguration pages.

claims.where: controls[1].api
claims.claim: RestrictTeamsSignInToAccountsFromTenantList is the documented Windows registry value and macOS com.microsoft.teams preference key for restricting desktop sign-in tenants.
claims.quote: Value Name: RestrictTeamsSignInToAccountsFromTenantList ... Domain: com.microsoft.teams ... Key: RestrictTeamsSignInToAccountsFromTenantList

claims.where: controls[1].ui
claims.claim: No admin-centre navigation path is documented for this desktop sign-in restriction policy.
claims.quote: Searched: 'RestrictTeamsSignInToAccountsFromTenantList admin center Intune configuration policy'; opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/sign-in-teams. Desktop instructions give GPO, registry and macOS plist configuration, not an admin-centre path.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The desktop sign-in restriction policy can be deployed through MDM or GPO.
claims.quote: The policies can be set via usual Device Management solutions such as MDM (Mobile Device Management) or GPO (Group Policy Object).

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The sign-in restriction does not prevent guest invitations or switching to tenants where the user is a guest.
claims.quote: It does not restrict the ability for users to be invited as a guest in other Microsoft Entra tenants, or switch to those other tenants (where users have been invited as a guest).

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The device policy restricts first and additional account sign-ins to accounts homed in allowlisted Microsoft Entra tenants, rather than directly controlling the panel.
claims.quote: When this policy is configured on a device, users can only sign in with accounts homed in a Microsoft Entra tenant that's included in the "Tenant Allow List" defined in the policy. The policy applies to all sign-ins, including first and additional accounts.

claims.quote: Viewing activity notifications in the panel doesn’t mark items as read

claims.claim: Notifications clear when clicked in the panel.
claims.quote: they clear when clicked in the panel or viewed in that tenant’s main Activity app.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure

claims.quote: they clear when clicked in the panel or viewed in that tenant’s main Activity app.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly specified whether guest tenants appear in this panel.
claims.quote: Searched: '"activity in other accounts" "guest"'; opened panel and sign-in pages. The panel page says accounts or organizations but does not explicitly identify guest tenants; the sign-in page's guest exception concerns the sign-in policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The panel documentation describes no automated action beyond surfacing notifications and opening them on a user's click.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams activity in other accounts orgs panel default disable admin policy PowerShell Graph guest tenants improvements'; read the full panel page. It describes notification display and user-selected interactions, not autonomous actions.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is recorded as unknown because no feature-specific licence requirement has been published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Replace the licensing explanation with: 'Manage Teams licenses states that, except for joining meetings anonymously, each user in your organisation needs a Teams licence to use Teams. No panel-specific licence requirement is published.' Replace 'has not stated ... any licence' in the summary with 'has not stated the improvements' default or a panel-specific licence requirement', and narrow the licensing question and cost rationale to feature-specific licensing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The panel's own Learn page names no licence or separate charge.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Teams license requirements use Teams user license activity other accounts organizations pricing' and '"activity in other accounts" licensing price meter'; opened the complete panel page and Manage Teams licenses. The panel page has no licensing or charging statement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No feature-specific meter is published for the panel.
claims.quote: Searched: '"activity in other accounts" licensing price meter' and 'Microsoft Teams license requirements use Teams user license activity other accounts organizations pricing'; opened the panel page and Manage Teams licenses. No panel meter was identified.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The roadmap record gives no pricing.
claims.quote: Stay up-to-date with what's happening in your other accounts and organizations with the 'Activity in Other Accounts and Orgs' panel.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Before this change users could see another tenant's activity only after switching tenants.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams notifications other accounts organizations before switching tenants activity panel'; read the panel page and Plan for multitenant organizations search excerpt. Neither establishes the claimed historical restriction; existing documentation describes cross-tenant notifications.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'For a service owner, the panel brings another tenant's activity notifications together in the main Teams window.' Remove 'rather than only after switching tenants'.

claims.where: Scope: Rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described rollout mechanics for the roadmap improvements.
claims.quote: Searched: '"activity in other accounts" improvements 577901 rollout prerequisites'; read the roadmap record and full preview panel page. They give a target and preview behaviour but no deployment sequence for the improvements.

claims.where: Scope: Rollout
claims.claim: No additional feature-specific prerequisite beyond multiple signed-in accounts is documented for these improvements.
claims.quote: Searched: '"activity in other accounts" improvements 577901 rollout prerequisites'; read the roadmap and panel page. Apart from desktop availability already stated in Scope and multiple signed-in accounts, no feature-specific prerequisite is listed.

claims.where: front matter: action; summary; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The review action rating fits a briefing about improvements to an existing user interface that tells administrators to prepare users before rollout.
claims.quote: action: "review"; 'tell them the panel and its notification previews are coming'; 'Brief the help desk on the 10-notification limit'.
claims.fix: Set action to 'prepare' and change 'admins should review it' in the summary to 'admins should prepare user communications'. The standard assigns prepare to a redesign of existing behaviour needing communication, even when its default state is unknown.
